item_verdicts.title: Masked full-frame pixelmatch diff over the 5 canonical states — the ONE orthogonal metric
item_verdicts.why: Sources hold: github.com/mapbox/pixelmatch confirms zero dependencies, raw typed arrays, 'just a few hundred lines', OKLab/HyAB perceptual distance, and accurate anti-aliased-pixel detection with includeAA; playwright.dev/docs/api/class-pageassertions confirms toHaveScreenshot's threshold is 'an acceptable perceived color difference in the YIQ color space… Defaults to 0.2' and maxDiffPixelRatio is 'an acceptable ratio of pixels that are different to the total amount of pixels'. Repo grounding holds: FIDELITY_GATE.md records the v1 14/17 FAIL and the slice-2b olive-band re-measurement; reference/ is gitignored (.gitignore line 9) and docs/MASTER_SPEC.md says 'Reference material stays local-only (reference/ gitignored) — the grant is to recreate, not to redistribute'; scripts/art/compareToSource.py exists as the build-time-only local diagnostic; tests/a6Score.test.ts states the sealed score 'runs in a clean clone with no reference/'. Frame timestamps check out in src/config/fidelity.ts probe notes (B t=3772-3776, B t=3771.55-3772.55, B t=3773.48-3773.65, B t=3783.2-3783.8, A t=3361-3364). TWO factual errors survive attack: the assertion count and, more seriously, the empirical basis offered for the threshold.
item_verdicts.correction: (1) The gate currently asserts 54 places, not 55: src/config/fidelity.ts holds 40 entries in FIDELITY_PROBES and 14 in FIDELITY_SCANS. FIDELITY_GATE.md's '55 assertions (41 points + 14 edge scans)' is stale relative to the config — cite the config, not the doc. (2) Strike 'the repo's own measured per-channel spreads of 16-26/255 land in this range'. The repo's recorded per-point SPREADS are ≤9 and mostly 0-6 ('zero spread', '≤1', '≤2', '≤3', '≤4', '≤6', and 'spreads ≤9' on the bar-gradient rows). 16-26 are the committed TOLERANCES (tol values in the file are 10, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26). So no measured spread justifies a 0.25-0.3 pixelmatch threshold. (3) pixelmatch's threshold is a normalized perceptual (OKLab) distance, not a per-channel /255 quantity, so there is no arithmetic conversion from a tol of 26 to a threshold value — the number must be ratchet-calibrated empirically from an actual run, exactly as the item's last sentence already says. Also note pixelmatch's OWN default threshold is 0.1 (README); 0.2 is Playwright's default, correctly attributed.

item_verdicts.title: pixelmatch/SSIM as the render-vs-render CI regression gate
item_verdicts.why: Verified in the repo. tests/poseRender.test.ts imports rasterDigest from scripts/art/rasterise and pins two SHA-256 goldens (GOLDEN_DRESSED = ebf871c5…, GOLDEN_IDLE = 6dae62d1…) in the 'GOLDEN: the dressed and idle renders still produce the same pixels' test. That file's own header states verbatim that the mutations it caught include 'shifting the sub-pixel sample from the centre to the corner, which moves the whole silhouette by an eighth of a pixel in one axis' and 'Math.floor → Math.round in the crop, which moves the frame by 1 px' — both exactly as the research claims, and both classes a tolerance diff is designed to forgive. scripts/art/rasterise.ts is a headless TS rasteriser with no GPU/font path, so an exact digest is achievable. The Playwright source backing the general 'standard practice' claim is confirmed (YIQ threshold, default 0.2, maxDiffPixelRatio). Adjudication survives intact; no action is the right call.

item_verdicts.title: Perceptual hashes (pHash/dHash) for fidelity gating
item_verdicts.why: The REJECT rests on repo facts, and every one checks out. tests/a6Score.test.ts's 'GATE A6-C companion — the fighter may not get TALLER' asserts overshoot > 0.10 and < 0.12 verbatim, with the comment '11 % too tall is a real, unfixed miss, pinned here so it cannot silently grow' — the 0.10-0.12 band is real, not paraphrase. The '≤26/255 color deltas' figure matches the maximum tol in src/config/fidelity.ts (tol values 10-26). The generic pHash/dHash property claimed (robust-by-design to scaling/compression/brightness; a hash match is a candidate, not identity) is uncontroversial and standard, and invariance to small differences is indeed the anti-goal for a gate whose job is catching a 6% drift. Nothing to refute.

item_verdicts.title: SSIM / MS-SSIM as an additional gate score
item_verdicts.why: The cited invariant exists and says what is claimed: FIDELITY_GATE.md's 'Adding probes (the rule)' requires measure-on-the-frames-first (median across ≥3 frames, record spread), a source-frame note in src/config/fidelity.ts, red-first, and 'Never widen a tolerance to make a probe pass — tolerances are codec headroom, not fudge room.' Per-point provenance is real — every probe in the config carries a note with its t= source. The alternative offered also exists: scripts/art/silhouette.ts exports widthProfile and profileAgreement over PROFILE_SAMPLES (19 heights), and tests/a6Score.test.ts holds it as ratcheted floors (FLOOR_TRACING 0.9005, FLOOR_HELDOUT 0.8490, plus a frame-to-frame ceiling test). The SSIM folklore thresholds quoted are not load-bearing for the REJECT, so the weak grade-C source behind them does not sink the item.

item_verdicts.title: CIEDE2000-derived tolerances for the lossless-PNG refinement pass, with chroma-aware headroom
item_verdicts.why: The repo half is clean: FIDELITY_GATE.md's v2 backlog does list 'Color refinement from lossless sources: the archived official-wiki PNGs … re-measure the palette against them and tighten tolerances', and src/core/fidelityCompare.ts is exactly per-channel max-delta (compareProbe takes Math.max of per-channel |expected − actual| against probe.tol) with only ONE/ZERO imported from config/nums — so 'derive offline, don't change the assertion math' is sound and cheap. The SOURCES are where this breaks. Fetching techkon.datacolor.com yields only 'a 1 DE00 is deemed the threshold… below it signifies an imperceptible difference' — it does NOT state the 1.0-2.0 trained-eye band or the 2.0-3.5 commercial-acceptability limit attributed to it. zschuessler.github.io/DeltaE/learn gives ≤1 not perceptible / 1-2 perceptible on close observation / 2-10 perceptible at a glance, explicitly declines to give a commercial threshold, and warns the scale is the author's own testing. So '2.0-3.5 the usual commercial acceptability limit' is attributed to sources that do not contain it. Worse, the 3dverse devlog cited for the codec half contains no codec-parameter content at all — it is a color-science primer on cone response, CIE XYZ and metamerism — and the Wikipedia chroma-subsampling article says nothing about quantization. And the specific mechanism claimed is backwards for H.264: chroma QP is derived from luma QP through a mapping table whose chroma range is capped BELOW luma's, i.e. chroma is quantized LESS coarsely, not harder.
item_verdicts.correction: Restate the claim as: 'CIEDE2000 (dE00) is the CIE-recommended perceptual color difference; dE00 ≈ 1.0 is the just-noticeable threshold (Techkon; corroborated by zschuessler's ≤1 not perceptible / 1-2 on close observation / 2-10 at a glance). Any tighter commercial-acceptability figure must be sourced separately — neither cited page supports 2.0-3.5. Separately, H.264 4:2:0 stores chroma at one quarter the sample count of luma (half horizontal AND half vertical), so video-derived color error is systematically larger in chroma than luma through SPATIAL AVERAGING AND BLEED, not through harsher quantization — H.264 in fact derives chroma QP from luma QP via a mapping table capped below the luma range. Cite the chroma-subsampling article for the sampling fact only; drop the 3dverse devlog, which is a color-science primer and contains no codec-parameter content.' The operational recommendation is unchanged and still stands: derive tol offline via dE00 ≈ 2, keep asymmetric headroom so chroma-heavy colors retain larger tol than near-gray ones.

item_verdicts.title: Temporal/animation fidelity metric (per-beat pose comparison)
item_verdicts.why: The structural diagnosis is right and the repo confirms it: the gate samples 5 frozen states (src/config/fidelity.ts state values are vs-intro 7, fight-splash 6, fighting 21, result-win 8, result-defeat 12) and tests/a6Score.test.ts scores static renderPoseWith poses only, so no gate in the repo grades motion. COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md §S24-A does exist and is titled 'The stroke lifecycle (the model every row below feeds)'. tests/config-values.test.ts exists as the config-pinned-scalar idiom to reduce to. BUT the item leans on the SESSION23 A11.4 15fps stepper as if it established the OG's animation truth, and the ledger's new 'Verify-pass corrections (2026-08-12)' block in §S24-H — which explicitly WINS over the §S24-B/C/E rows — reverses exactly that reading.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace the A11.4 justification with the ledger's own 2026-08-12 verify-pass correction #4: the 27/55 rhythm is NOT a game-side stride but 'the OG's internal update quantum (~27.4 px) beating against the 15 fps capture', and the 60fps '4-frame content block' defence is 'VOID — that is a property of the capture (§00), not of the game'. The ruling is: 'build the Sim mover constant-speed at 60 Hz; compare fidelity at capture level (15 fps sampling), where the quantization reappears on its own. Do NOT hand-author a 27/55 stepper into core.' So the 15 fps floor is a MEASUREMENT limit, not the animation model — a temporal gate must assert 60 Hz sim scalars and only DOWNSAMPLE to 15 fps for comparison. The extraction pass must also inherit the block's corrected numbers: dash modelled as constant-speed line-follow ~616 px/s @1080 (~274 world px/s), range ~40-49 px/tick, plus a terminal contact snap of +139-192 px in one tick; run core quoted 573-685 px/s @1080; HEAVY stroke band 146-~275.

item_verdicts.title: Canvas screenshot flake control checklist
item_verdicts.why: Every element of the checklist is present in src/game/fidelity.ts as claimed: settleFrames(game, frames) awaits real frames with an explicit manual game.loop.step(performance.now()) fallback documented as the rAF-throttle failure class; snapshot() calls settleFrames then game.renderer.snapshot(...); FIGHTING_SETTLE_MS = 4000 is advanced through the sim rather than wall-clock; devHoldAt('vs' | 'fight') freezes the intro beats; and localStorage is backed up key-by-key and restored wholesale around the result state. FIDELITY_GATE.md slice 2b independently confirms the font-flake elimination: 'the VS and FIGHT! glyphs are procedural brush polygons/bars whose strokes pass through the measured probe points', after 'Georgia's V gap, then the F serif/slant' forced two render fixes. The Argos source (dev.to/jsfez) does carry the advice attributed to it — full resource load, pausing/removing animations, hiding dynamic content, fixed datasets, CI-standardized environments — though it is DOM-only and says nothing about WebGL or preserveDrawingBuffer; that half of the claim comes from the webglfundamentals citation, which is the appropriate source for it. The 'no action, reuse the existing snapshot()/settleFrames path' conclusion is correct.

overall_note: Attack summary: 4 of 7 items survive intact, 3 need corrections; none is refutable. No cited URL was dead or fabricated — all six I fetched resolved. The two ADAPT items (1 and 5) are the ones carrying real errors, and both errors are of the same kind: a number or mechanism asserted with more confidence than the evidence behind it supports. Item 1's '16-26/255 measured spreads' conflates the config's TOLERANCES with its recorded SPREADS (which are ≤9, mostly 0-6) — this matters because it was offered as the empirical basis for the proposed pixelmatch threshold, and it is not one; the threshold must be ratchet-calibrated from an actual run with no prior. Item 5's grade-B Techkon and 3dverse citations do not contain the claims hung on them (the dE00 2.0-3.5 acceptability band, and any codec/quantization content at all), and the 'chroma quantized harder than luma' mechanism is backwards for H.264 — though the recommendation survives because 4:2:0's spatial subsampling alone gets you there. Item 6 is the only one hit by the new ledger block, and per the brief that is not the research agent's fault: the 2026-08-12 verify-pass corrections in §S24-H landed after the research ran and explicitly forbid hand-authoring a 15fps/27-55 stepper into core, which is the opposite of what A11.4's commit title suggests — anyone building on item 6 must read that block first. Two incidental staleness findings in the repo, not in the research: FIDELITY_GATE.md says '55 assertions (41 points + 14 edge scans)' while src/config/fidelity.ts now holds 40 + 14 = 54, and the doc's v2 backlog still lists 'Bar gradients' as not-yet-asserted although the config now carries four hp/chi gradient probes and a BAR_GRADIENTS export. Worth a doc-refresh commit independent of this research.
